## Objective

Identify what already satisfies the approved TRD and record the starting state against which any repair will be judged.

## Scope

- The approved TRD, existing adoption receipt, live guidance and protected paths.

## Entry conditions

- The user has approved the exact plan revision and separately authorized the execution scope.

## Exit criteria

- Each approved criterion has an owner, location and planned check. Historical results and current observations are labeled.
- The baseline identifies current digests, existing work and the precise files eligible for conditional repair.

## Risks

- An existing adoption can be replayed accidentally. Use its exact receipt and the live files to determine the needed work.

## TASK-001 - Compare the approved requirements with the working tree

Read revision 2 of the TRD and the prior adoption record. For each criterion, identify the live source, Template or depot owner and the evidence needed at execution. Capture the initial state of the selected and protected paths before any edit.

### Risks

- A dirty worktree can hide an existing local edit. Record its starting bytes and keep unrelated changes outside the patch.

### Acceptance criteria

- The approved TRD ID and digest match the selected source, and all fifteen acceptance criteria are represented.
- All seven recorded source, Template and depot file sets have a current comparison. Each difference identifies its owner, cause if known and affected criterion.
- Every protected path and unrelated working edit has a preservation reference appropriate to its scope.

### Planned verification

- Reopen the TRD and receipt, compare their SHA-256 values and map each criterion to the relevant work and verification.
- Compare working bytes with the receipt's separate source_adopted and root_adopted pins, inspect the scoped Git diff, and record the state of each protected entry. Use a read-only inventory for product boundaries.
- If the comparison identifies a patch, capture the affected root and Template checks before changing the files so later regressions can be attributed to the patch.
